CVE-2026-102703.title: arbitrary read/write via grant copy
CVE-2026-102703.description:
[This CNA information record relates to multiple CVEs; the
text explains which aspects/vulnerabilities correspond to which CVE.]

A common access pattern is a batch of Grant Copy operations acting on
adjacent address ranges in the same source or destination page. For
performance reasons, Xen caches details internally to reuse already
validated data. The conditions on when to re-validate the internal data
were not correct in some cases:

- Frame numbers and grant references could wrongly be mixed up. This
is CVE-2026-102703.

- Copying by frame number (rather than grant reference) is permitted
only when operating on the caller's own memory. The check to enforce
this restriction was misplaced. This is CVE-2026-102704.

CVE-2026-119202.title: @hapi/content: quadratic-time parsing of Content-Disposition parameters allows denial of service
CVE-2026-119202.description: @hapi/content provides HTTP Content-* header parsing. From 3.0.6 until 6.0.3, Content.disposition() uses an unanchored parameter-name expression in a global regular-expression scan, causing repeated failed matching over the remaining input when a Content-Disposition parameter contains a long token without an equals sign. The resulting quadratic processing can block the Node.js event loop before route handlers or validation when @hapi/pez parses multipart/form-data headers, including unauthenticated hapi routes with payload.multipart enabled, and also affects applications that pass untrusted headers directly to Content.disposition(). This issue is fixed in @hapi/content version 6.0.3.

CVE-2026-129182.title: Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown
CVE-2026-129182.description:
Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown.

A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repopulate the stored fatal error backtrace after the executor has been cleaned up. The request memory is then freed, and a diagnostic emitted before executor initialization in a later request handled by the same PHP-FPM or mod_php worker can access the stale backtrace. The shutdown error requires per-path configuration of max_memory_limit, or of zlib.output_compression together with output_handler (which .user.ini can also set). The early diagnostic requires Apache per-directory configuration or, for PHP-FPM, a PHP_VALUE or PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameter sent by the front end. This can cause memory corruption and worker crashes, and may allow remote code execution.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

This makes it possible for attackers (with access to a valid MCP bearer token) to escalate privileges to the token owner's Administrator role — bypassing NHI ability allow-list and scope restrictions entirely — by submitting any valid MCP bearer token (including scope-restricted connection-test tokens) to arbitrary WordPress endpoints such as admin-ajax.php. This requires possession of a valid MCP bearer token, which is routinely issued to any administrator who connects an MCP client to the site. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

CVE-2026-55614.title: uhttpd vulnerable to HTTP request smuggling via case-sensitive Transfer-Encoding matching
CVE-2026-55614.description: uhttpd is a small HTTP server. In unpatched repository snapshots, `client_parse_header()` in `client.c` lowercases header names but compares the `Transfer-Encoding` value to `chunked` using case-sensitive `strcmp`. A mixed-case transfer-coding token is accepted without enabling `r->transfer_chunked`, despite transfer-coding tokens being case-insensitive. On a keep-alive connection, the `chunked` POST body is left unread and request-shaped body bytes are parsed as another HTTP request, permitting HTTP request smuggling and boundary desynchronization. Commits ae015e099986ceace44975cb69629841a2d58d37 and 6641b050e5f7c7fd9ae92e8e119d6d6dfc6e9837 patch the issue.

CVE-2026-99324.title: ksmbd: fix out-of-bounds read when padding the final compound response
CVE-2026-99324.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix out-of-bounds read when padding the final compound response

Compound response handling pads the last response of a compound to an
8-byte boundary by growing the final iov and the RFC1002 length.
smb2_allocate_rsp_buf() allocates exactly response_sz. A command can
fill the response buffer to within 7 bytes of its end, for example a
QUERY_INFO whose output is bounded only by the space left. The padding
can then run past the allocation, and ksmbd_tcp_writev() reads those
bytes when it sends the response.

BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in _copy_from_iter+0x744/0x10e0
Call Trace:
_copy_from_iter+0x744/0x10e0
tcp_sendmsg_locked+0x2290/0x3f80
ksmbd_tcp_writev+0x10c7/0x1ab0 [ksmbd]

Allocate room for the padding when the request is a compound, as
smb2_read() and smb2_read_pipe() do for their payloads. response_sz is
unchanged, so commands still fill only up to it, and kvzalloc() zeroes
the padding.
